capture.final_message:
Prove the two conjuncts independently.

- For the polynomial identity, set
  \[
  A_n=S_n(2\cosh\theta)\sinh\theta,\qquad
  B_n=\sinh((n+1)\theta).
  \]
  The Chebyshev recurrence and the hyperbolic addition formula show that both integer-indexed sequences satisfy
  \[
  X_{n+1}=2\cosh(\theta)X_n-X_{n-1}.
  \]
  Verify two consecutive initial values, conveniently \(n=-1,0\). Since the recurrence is reversible, equality follows for every \(n\in\mathbb Z\). Keeping the factor \(\sinh\theta\) avoids any invalid division when \(\sinh\theta=0\).

- For the arithmetic estimate, use the prime-power decomposition
  \[
  \psi(x)-\theta(x)=\sum_{k\ge2}\theta(x^{1/k})
  \]
  for \(x\ge2\). Apply a Chebyshev upper bound \(\theta(y)\le A y\). The \(k=2\) term is \(O(\sqrt x)\), while
  \[
  \sum_{k\ge3}x^{1/k}\le O(x^{1/3}\log x)=O(\sqrt x).
  \]
  Absorb the bounded range \(x<2\) into the constant; for nonpositive \(x\), the counting functions vanish and \(\sqrt x=0\) in Lean’s real-square-root convention. Thus one universal \(C\) works.
